title: Five traits, or you pay the price
heading: A brilliant freelancer with amnesia, every time
caption: Five traits to manage, or you pay the price.

probabilistic.name: Probabilistic
probabilistic.freelancer: Give the same brief to a new freelancer, and get a different plan.
probabilistic.ai: <marker>Give the same prompt in a new chat, and get a different answer.</marker>
probabilistic.popover: The same brief can come back different every time. It picks a likely answer, not a fixed one, so one good result is not a promise.

relentless.name: Relentless
relentless.freelancer: Hand over the job, and they work day and night, producing stacks of polished pages, whether they’re right or not.
relentless.ai: <marker>Send the prompt, and it produces pages in seconds, as many as you ask for, whether they’re right or not.</marker>
relentless.popover: Pages pour out fast and polished, whether they are right or not. There is a lot to read, and all of it needs checking.

informed.name: Informed
informed.freelancer: Ask a freelancer who knows every trade, and get expert answers, blind to your company and culture.
informed.ai: <marker>Ask AI, trained on more text than anyone could read, and get the likeliest answer, blind to your company and culture.</marker>
informed.popover: It knows a great deal about the world and nothing about your company. Your culture and unwritten rules never reached it.

confident.name: Confident
confident.freelancer: Give a vague request, and they start without asking, fill the gaps with their own assumptions, and sell it to you as right.
confident.ai: <marker>Give a vague prompt, and it starts without asking, fills the gaps with the most common answers, and replies with full confidence.</marker>
confident.popover: It starts instead of asking, and fills the gaps with guesses. A guess sounds as sure as a fact.

every-word-billed.name: Every word billed
every-word-billed.freelancer: They bill every word they read and write, so one more question means paying to reread the whole file, their own pages included.
every-word-billed.ai: <marker>It charges for every word it reads and writes, so one more message means paying for the whole chat again, its own answers included.</marker>
every-word-billed.popover: Every new question pays again for all the words so far. The longer it runs, the bigger the bill.

backs.turn: Turn the card to its text

closing: Amnesia: after each conversation, they forget everything, so you have to onboard them again, and every job starts from zero.

right-or-not-the-output-looks-finished.header: Right or not, the output looks finished
right-or-not-the-output-looks-finished.description: even state-of-the-art models "still regularly produce logical mistakes", which is why speed without checking is a trap [1].

lightman-verify-step-by-step.title: Lightman et al., Let's Verify Step by Step

probable-not-random.description: text generation samples from a probability distribution rather than always picking the single likeliest word, because the always-likeliest text is bland and repetitive [1]. Even with randomness set to zero the provider documents that "the results will not be fully deterministic" [2].

holtzman-text-degeneration.title: Holtzman et al., The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration

how-much-varies.description: in one test 1,000 completions of one prompt at zero randomness gave 80 unique answers [1]. Across five models set up for determinism, accuracy moved by up to 15% between runs of the same task [2].

he-defeating-nondeterminism.title: He et al., Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference

atil-deterministic-settings.title: Atil et al., Non-Determinism of "Deterministic" LLM Settings

the-bill-covers-the-whole-chat.header: The bill covers the whole chat
the-bill-covers-the-whole-chat.description: the interface is stateless: the earlier turns go in with every request, and the model's own answers become part of the next input [1]. Each resent word is billed as input [2].

a-discount-not-an-exemption.description: cached reads cost about a tenth of base input, the default cache lasts 5 minutes, and caching changes what is paid, not whether the words count toward the window [1].

why-it-guesses-instead-of-asking.header: Why it guesses instead of asking
why-it-guesses-instead-of-asking.description: most benchmarks score a guess above an abstention, so training rewards guessing [1]. Current models rarely ask for clarification and answer wrongly instead [2].

kalai-why-models-hallucinate.title: Kalai et al., Why Language Models Hallucinate

kuhn-clam.title: Kuhn et al., CLAM: Selective Clarification for Ambiguous Questions with Generative Language Models

why-it-is-blind-to-your-company.header: Why it is blind to your company
why-it-is-blind-to-your-company.description: a model's accuracy on a fact relates to how many documents about it it saw in training [1], and a leading model family was trained on publicly available data alone [2]. The provider states it does not train on commercial inputs and outputs by default [3].

kandpal-long-tail-knowledge.title: Kandpal et al., Large Language Models Struggle to Learn Long-Tail Knowledge

touvron-llama.title: Touvron et al., LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

anthropic-training-data.title: Anthropic, Is my data used for model training? (commercial products)

the-forgetting-is-in-the-design.header: The forgetting is in the design
the-forgetting-is-in-the-design.description: the context window is described as the model's "working memory", distinct from the corpus it was trained on [1]. Memory across chats exists only where an application stores notes and puts them back, since the memory tool runs client-side [2].

who-gets-the-job.title: Who gets the job
who-gets-the-job.script: Now imagine you hand this job to a freelancer: brilliant, but with amnesia. And they come with five weird traits.

probabilistic-relentless.title: Probabilistic, Relentless
probabilistic-relentless.script: One: they're probabilistic. Ask them the same question twice, and you get a slightly different answer, sometimes a very different one. Two: they're relentless. No bathroom breaks, no sleep, fully locked on whatever task you give them.

informed.title: Informed
informed.script: Three: they're very informed. A degree in every subject you can imagine. But they know nothing about you, your company, your culture or your processes.

confident-every-word-billed.title: Confident, Every word billed
confident-every-word-billed.script: Four: they're extremely confident, to the point that they'll sell you their answer as correct. Five: they bill you for every word they hear from you, and every word they say.
